canonical_decision.quote:
A recent genome-wide association study by the International Multiple Sclerosis Genetics Consortium (IMSGC) reported
association of 17 single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in 14 loci with multiple sclerosis (MS). Only two loci, HLA-DRA
and IL2RA, reached genome-wide significance (Po5E08). In our study, we determined whether we could replicate the results
of the IMSGC and whether more SNPs are genome-wide significantly associated with MS. We assessed the association between
the 17 IMSGC SNPs and MS in three cohorts (total number of subjects 3981, among these 1853 cases). We performed a
meta-analysis of the results of our study, the original IMSGC results and the results of a recent replication study performed in
the Australian population. Of the 17 IMSGC SNPs, five SNPs showed genome-wide significant association with MS: HLA-DRA
(P¼8E124), IL7R (P¼6E09), IL2RA (P¼1E11), CD58 (P¼4E09) and CLEC16A (P¼3E12).Therefore, genome-wide
significance has now been shown for SNPs in different non-HLA MS risk genes.
canonical_decision.reason: Hoppenbrouwers et al. (2009) tested all 17 top candidate SNPs reported in the initial IMSGC (2007, 10.1056/nejmoa073493) genome-wide association study across three independent multiple sclerosis cohorts and a combined analysis of 11,376 individuals. While 5 SNPs reached genome-wide significance (HLA-DRA, IL7R, IL2RA, CD58, and CLEC16A) and EVI5 was independently replicated, the remaining tested IMSGC SNPs did not reach genome-wide significance, and for three IMSGC loci (PDE4B, DBC1, and ANKRD15) the authors explicitly report on p. 677 that 'our results suggest that the previously reported association in the initial IMSGC screen was a false positive association.' Because some tested original loci from IMSGC (2007) replicated and others failed as false positives, the paper-level outcome is mixed.

canonical_decision.quote:
Recently, significant linkage has been
reported to a 39.5 cM region on the long arm of chromosome 2 (2q36-37; PARK11) in North American
Parkinson families under an autosomal dominant model of inheritance. We have performed a replication
study to confirm linkage to this region in a European population. Linkage analysis in 153 individuals from
45 European families with a strong family history of PD did not show any significant LOD score in this
region. Therefore, PARK11 does not seem to play a major role for familial PD in the European population.

canonical_decision.quote:
The finding that the fraction problem distributions in Swiss textbooks partly diverge from U.S.

patterns (as identified by Braithwaite & Siegler) provides an additional opportunity to evaluate

the associative learning hypothesis. Given that most Swiss children’s responses in the

Fraction-Test of Study 2 reflected specific patterns in their Swiss textbooks—differing from

the patterns identified in U.S. mathematics textbooks—supports the associative learning

hypothesis. Specifically, in Tasks 1 and 2, when Swiss children saw the operation +/-, they

produced more often two fractions with unequal denominators rather than with equal

denominators. This specific unbalanced presentation of tasks in Swiss textbook is not

present in U.S. textbooks and was not found in U.S. children’s associations. Thus, our results

provide additional empirical support that associations of children reflect their textbook task

pattern rather than inherent features of fraction arithmetic.
canonical_decision.reason: Independent parent full current-body reading supports successful for the specified2018input-dependent associative-learning finding. The authors explicitly design Swiss/U.S.problem-distribution differences to distinguish learned textbook associations from inherent arithmetic preferences, state that the observed Swiss-specific response pattern supports this original claim, and conclude Overall these results complement Braithwaite/Siegler2018. Abstract and GeneralDiscussion describe the two-study conceptual replication positively. Thus differing ambient textbook cell frequencies are the intended cross-context test of the conditional learning claim, not an original requirement that every country reproduce U.S.frequency cells.
